skill.name: prisma-postgres
skill.description: Prisma Postgres setup and operations guidance across Console, create-db CLI, Management API, and Management API SDK. Use when creating Prisma Postgres databases, working in Prisma Console, provisioning with create-db/create-pg/create-postgres, or integrating programmatic provisioning with service tokens or OAuth.
skill.summary: Provision and manage Prisma Postgres through Console, CLI, Management API, or TypeScript SDK workflows.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: Static matches for database URLs, environment variables, official Prisma endpoints, and Markdown backticks are benign documentation examples rather than secret collection or command injection. The source contains no prompt injection or unauthorized exfiltration behavior. Separate semantic review identified unpinned npm execution and API keys passed in command arguments as risks requiring remediation.

remediation.issue: Commands execute npm packages through unpinned @latest tags, and some Prisma CLI examples suppress confirmation with -y.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions, publish expected integrity details, and require user confirmation before downloaded packages execute.

remediation.issue: Non-interactive link examples place an API key directly in command-line arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use interactive authentication or a supported environment, standard input, or secure CI secret mechanism. Explicitly require log redaction and key rotation.

remediation.issue: Connection and claim URLs are written to local environment files without complete file-protection guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to exclude secret files from version control, restrict file permissions, use secret stores in production, and rotate exposed credentials.

content.value_statement: Prisma Postgres setup spans several tools, authentication models, and connection methods. This skill selects the right workflow and provides focused operational guidance.
actual_capabilities: Compare Console, create-db CLI, Management API, and SDK workflows.
Provide CLI commands for temporary and project-owned database provisioning.
Explain project linking and DATABASE_URL setup for Prisma applications.
Outline service-token and OAuth authentication flows for Management API integrations.
Describe direct and pooled connection endpoints plus recommended Node.js adapters.
Show typed SDK setup for existing tokens and OAuth token refresh.
limitations: Does not execute commands, provision resources, or verify live account state by itself.
Requires valid Prisma account permissions, tokens, and workspace access.
Examples use latest npm package tags unless users pin reviewed versions.
OAuth token storage and callback security require application-specific implementation.

use_cases.title: Create Preview Databases
use_cases.description: Choose a region, set a lifecycle, and obtain connection details for development, demonstrations, or temporary CI environments.

use_cases.title: Automate Platform Provisioning
use_cases.description: Plan service-token or OAuth workflows for creating and managing workspace, project, branch, and database resources.

use_cases.title: Connect Existing Projects
use_cases.description: Link a local Prisma project, configure DATABASE_URL, select an adapter, and prepare schema generation or migration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Development Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a temporary Prisma Postgres database in [region]. Explain lifecycle, claim behavior, and safe connection-string handling before suggesting commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a temporary development database

prompt_templates.title: Link an Existing Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan how to link my local Prisma project to database [database ID]. Include interactive and CI options without exposing API keys in arguments.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate local and CI project configuration

prompt_templates.title: Design Service-Token Provisioning
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a service-token provisioning flow for workspace [name]. Cover resource hierarchy, endpoint selection, credential storage, retries, and least privilege.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced backend automation with the Management API

prompt_templates.title: Review Multi-Tenant OAuth
prompt_templates.prompt: Review an OAuth-based multi-tenant Prisma Management API architecture. Address state, PKCE verifier storage, token refresh, tenant isolation, audit logs, and secret rotation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert security review for a production platform integration

output_examples.input: Create a temporary database in Europe for a pull request preview.
output: Select eu-central-1 or eu-west-3 based on application latency and policy.
Set a short lifetime that covers the review window.
Keep the connection and claim URLs out of logs and source control.
Claim the database only when the preview must become persistent.

output_examples.input: Should a Node.js service use a direct or pooled Prisma Postgres endpoint?
output_examples.output: Use the direct endpoint with the PostgreSQL adapter for a standard long-running Node.js service. Consider pooled or serverless options only when runtime constraints require them.

output_examples.input: Outline a secure OAuth SDK integration for customer workspaces.
output: Register an exact callback URL and request only required scopes.
Store OAuth state and the PKCE verifier securely before redirecting.
Persist encrypted tokens with strict tenant ownership checks.
Rotate refresh tokens, redact logs, and clear tokens during logout.

best_practices: Pin npm package versions and review release notes before running provisioning commands.
Keep service tokens, API keys, claim URLs, and database URLs in an approved secret store.
Use least privilege, confirm the target workspace, and protect one-time connection details from logs.
anti_patterns: Do not place API keys directly in shell commands, chat messages, or CI logs.
Do not run destructive restore or removal operations without exact resource confirmation and backups.
Do not treat temporary databases, placeholder token storage, or example callback URLs as production defaults.

faq.question: Does this skill create databases automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and examples. Resource creation still requires an authorized Prisma account, reviewed commands, and network access.

faq.question: Which provisioning method should I choose?
faq.answer: Use Console for manual work, create-db for temporary instances, Platform CLI for project resources, and Management API for application automation.

faq.question: Are create-db databases permanent?
faq.answer: They are temporary by default and usually expire after about 24 hours. Use the claim flow when you need persistence.

faq.question: How should Management API authentication work?
faq.answer: Use a service token for your workspace. Use OAuth when acting for users across workspaces, with secure state, verifier, and token storage.

faq.question: Can I connect from serverless runtimes?
faq.answer: Yes. Select the serverless driver and adapter only when runtime constraints require them. Standard Node.js services usually use direct PostgreSQL connections.

faq.question: How should I protect database credentials?
faq.answer: Use a secret store, restrict file access, exclude local environment files from version control, redact logs, and rotate any exposed credential.
